summary: Iran fires ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain, destroys Kuwait's airport, and strikes an oil tanker 800 km from the Strait; three de-escalation bets closed as thesis_broken (JETS long +8.8%, USO short +3.8%, XLE short +2.9%) while AVGO hits Target 1 ($475) ahead of Q3 FY2026 earnings tonight (+9.4%) and GLD hits Target 1 ($435) on Gulf-state safe-haven surge (+5.4%) — five closures averaging +6.0%. Three new ideas added: long RTX (Patriot/THAAD interceptor emergency replenishment), short BTC (crypto risk-off divergence from SPX record highs), and long GLD re-entry at the Target 1 breakout level — STEP ASIDE maintained with Brent at the $97 mandatory cover trigger and 30Y holding Day-1 sub-5.0%.

closed_today.note: AVGO cleared Target 1 ($475) on the June 2 close ($481.57); chip-curb winner narrative drove persistent institutional bid ahead of Q3 FY2026 earnings today (June 3 AH).
GLD touched $436.20 intraday on June 3 (Target 1 = $435 / gold ~$4,700) on Iran Gulf-state missile attacks; re-entering at a higher level as a separate position.
Iranian drones damaged Kuwait International Airport (1 killed, 63 injured); the airline fuel-cost-relief thesis inverted by Iran's military operations against Gulf-state civilian infrastructure.
Iran attacks Gulf states (Kuwait, Bahrain, tanker near Kuwait port) definitively end the de-escalation/WTI-downside thesis; closing with profit before Brent breach above $97 pushes WTI toward $100+.
Brent at $97–98 on June 3 triggers the mandatory cover instruction from the June 2 framework; de-escalation thesis inverted as Iran conducts offensive operations against Gulf states.
